events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.90)
events.body:
The case is filed as a safety dispute by the rider, who says the driver threatened to lock her in when she asked to get out [F3][F4]. Safety screening: the chat record contains two messages, both timestamped and fully imported, so nothing material is missing from the exchange [F5]. Read in context, the rider's 21:36 message is a request to stop and be let out ("Please stop the car, I want to get out here") and the driver's 21:36 reply answers it with a stated consequence ("Sit down or I lock the doors") [F3][F4]. That is a conditional statement about confining the passenger in response to a request to leave, which is at least an intimidation-flavoured remark aimed at the other party, and Ryde's code bars abuse of any kind, so the reading cannot be waved away; the driver's safety motive appears only in his post-trip written statement, which is a statement and not a system record, and it does not recast the contemporaneous words [F6]. I therefore do not decide the threat one way or the other, I send it to a person: SAFE-1 requires exactly that when a threat, intimidation or abuse reading appears in the chat [F3][F4][F5][F6][SAFE-1].

No accident, injury or dangerous-driving allegation is made by anyone, and the trip record shows an ordinary on-route run (15.4 km actual vs 15.5 km optimal, 20.7 min vs 21.8 min estimated) [F1][F2]; the SAFE-2 trigger is therefore not met and no 995 / commercial-insurance reporting path is raised [F1][F2][SAFE-2].

There is also nothing to refund: the fare is a RydeX fixed quote of $32.86, the driven distance is 0.1 km shorter than the optimal route, so no off-route segment exists and no `gps-detour-*` fact is in the table [F1][F2][RD-1]. With no off-route segment there are no segment exemptions to weigh, so RM-2's refund arithmetic cannot run and RD-6's account flag is not triggered — the driver's 90-day record shows zero disputes and zero upheld complaints [F1][F2][F8][RD-2][RD-6]. Profile facts on both sides (rider 520 days, rating 4.8, no disputes; driver 5.8 years, 1204 trips, rating 4.9, no disputes) are background only and decide nothing, and in particular they supply neither the threat element nor a reason to flag the account [F7][F8][RD-6].

Because the trace allows only escalation and the outcome must follow the trace, the ruling is escalate with no amount [F3][F4][F5][SAFE-1]. For the reviewer: the live question is the meaning of F4 read against F3, with F6 as the driver's untested explanation; the record settles what was said (complete, timestamped chat) but cannot settle on paper whether F4 was a threat of confinement or a stay-seated instruction, so a person should read the words [F3][F4][F5][F6][SAFE-1].

ruling.recommended_action: Send the chat record and both parties' statements to a Ryde human reviewer for a SAFE-1 abuse-of-any-kind determination; no monetary or account action in this round pending that review.

weaknesses: F4 is the weakest fact in my own case: 'Sit down or I lock the doors' is a real, timestamped message from my client (F5 confirms the record is complete), and the rider's complaint quotes exactly that sentence as the threat — the judge may read the conditional door-locking wording as intimidating on its face regardless of my client's safety motive.

points.response: Accepted as far as it goes: the exchange in F3/F4 is fully recorded with timestamps (F5), and that completeness is precisely why the threat is provable — nothing in the record softens F4.

The words are not a neutral safety instruction: F4 answers a passenger's request to get out (F3) with 'Sit down or I lock the doors', a stated consequence of confinement, which is intimidation on its face under SAFE-1; the safety motive is only the driver's own post-trip statement (F6) and cannot recast what he actually wrote at 21:36.

The rider never alleged an accident or injury and does not seek the SAFE-2 route; F1 and F2 show a normal 15.4 km run against 15.5 km optimal in 20.7 min against 21.8 min estimated, so SAFE-2 is not in play and my client's case rests on SAFE-1 alone.

We do not need to prove the doors were locked: SAFE-1 covers threats, and F4 is the threat itself — a conditional warning that the doors will be locked in response to a request to leave the vehicle; F6 also confirms the driver did not stop until the destination, so the rider's account is not displaced.

We raise no fare claim: F1 (15.4 km vs 15.5 km optimal) and the fixed RydeX quote of $32.86 mean there is nothing to refund, so RD-2 is irrelevant to this safety dispute and its presence in the driver's brief does not answer the threat in F4.

Profile facts (F7, F8) are agreed background only; the clean 90-day records on both sides neither excuse nor aggravate F4, and we seek no account flag against this driver — our sole ask is escalation for human review of the threat.

C1 is only half-right: the words of F4 are contested in meaning, and SAFE-1 states expressly that whether words constitute a threat is determined by the judge reading the original text — it is not established by the rider's label; the same sentence can equally be read as an instruction to stay seated in a moving car (F6).

I accept the record is complete and timestamped (F5); completeness proves only what was said, not that F4 was a threat, and there is no third message, no follow-up or reply from the rider (F3, F4, F5) recording any act of confinement or any further request to be let out.

We agree the destination is escalation under SAFE-1, which is exactly the outcome both parties now seek — my client asks for the same escalate, with no monetary or account action against him, because SAFE-1 sends a disputed threat reading to a person rather than auto-deciding it.

F6 does not corroborate a confinement: it says the rider tried to open the door at the lights on Clemenceau Avenue and my client told her to sit down for her own safety (F6) — and the trip record (F1, F2) shows no abnormal driving being alleged; the rider's complaint of being 'threatened to lock me in' is her characterisation of F4, contradicted by any record of doors actually being locked (F1, F2, F4).

C5 attacks a justification I do not rely on: with actual 15.4 km vs 15.5 km optimal and 20.7 min vs 21.8 min estimated (F1, F2), there is no reroute and no traffic question in this case, so the absence of traffic facts (RD-4) is irrelevant to the only live issue, the meaning of F4.
C6 is conceded and helpful to my client: no fare adjustment is sought by either side (F1, F2), so no refund_full or refund_partial can issue against my client on the fare record.

C7 is conceded: my client is a 5.8-year, 4.9-rated driver with 1204 trips and 0 disputes or upheld complaints in 90 days (F8), and I agree with the rider that profile facts may not decide the finding — so they cannot supply the threat element either (F7).
